# smtp-tester — full reference

> A local SMTP server that captures mail instead of delivering it, with a web inbox, an RFC
> compliance validator and an MCP server. It occupies MailHog/Mailpit's ports (1025 SMTP,
> 8025 HTTP) and adds validation and an agent-facing tool surface. It ships as one container.
> There is no library artifact and no Maven plugin: see "Not built, deliberately" at the end.

---

## 1. Running it

```bash
docker run --rm -p 1025:1025 -p 8025:8025 ghcr.io/sparrowlogic/smtp-tester
```

Point the application under test at `localhost:1025`. Nothing leaves the process: every message is
stored, parsed and validated, and no upstream delivery is ever attempted.

`AUTH` accepts any username and password by default, so a mail configuration that insists on
credentials works unchanged. STARTTLS is off by default and can be switched to `OPTIONAL` or
`REQUIRED`; a self-signed certificate is minted at startup unless you supply a keystore.

To persist captured mail across restarts, mount a volume at `/data/mail`. To run entirely in
memory, set `SMTP_TESTER_SPOOL_DIRECTORY=` (empty).

### Security posture

The inbox, the REST API and the MCP endpoint are **unauthenticated by design**, and SMTP accepts
any credentials. This is a local testing tool; the control is not exposing the ports, not a
password. Everything the UI displays arrived over SMTP from whatever could reach port 1025, so it
is treated as hostile: message bodies are served only under `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`,
message ids are validated before they can become a filesystem path, and the SMTP password is never
logged at any level.

---

## 2. Verifying a message from a test

The reliable sequence is subscribe-then-act, not act-then-sleep:

1. `GET /api/v1/messages/stream` and wait for the `ready` event.
2. Trigger the behaviour that sends the mail.
3. Wait for a `mail.received` event, whose `data` is the same JSON as `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}`.

If polling is easier, `GET /api/v1/messages?inbox=<address>` returns newest-first and is cheap.
Poll with a timeout that fails loudly rather than a fixed sleep. The recipient filter is called
`inbox`, not `to`.

An idle stream receives a `:keep-alive` comment every 20 seconds and is never timed out by the
server, so waiting minutes for a nightly job is as safe as waiting milliseconds in a unit test.
Beyond `smtp-tester.web.stream.max-subscribers` concurrent streams the endpoint answers `503`.

Two different things replay missed mail, and they are not interchangeable. `?since=` takes an
**ISO-8601 instant** and replays everything received at or after it, which is what covers mail sent
in the moment between deciding to subscribe and the subscription opening. The `Last-Event-ID`
request header takes a **message id** and is what a browser's `EventSource` sends automatically on
reconnect. Either way the replay is capped at `smtp-tester.web.stream.replay-limit` messages. An
unparseable `since` is rejected rather than ignored.

---

## 3. REST API

All paths are relative to `smtp-tester.web.base-path`, which is empty by default.

| Method and path | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/inboxes` | every recipient address with message and failure counts |
| `GET /api/v1/messages` | search by `inbox`, `from`, `subject`, `text`, `since`, `onlyFailed`, `limit` (default 50), `offset` |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}` | one parsed message with its validation findings |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/validation` | the findings alone |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/raw` | the exact bytes received, `message/rfc822` |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/html` | the HTML part, under a sandbox CSP |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/attachments/{index}` | one attachment, with its own content type |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/stream` | server-sent events: `ready`, then `mail.received`; same filters, plus `Last-Event-ID` |
| `DELETE /api/v1/messages/{id}` | delete one message |
| `DELETE /api/v1/messages` | delete everything, or one inbox with `?inbox=` |
| `GET /api/v1/tls/certificate` | the presented certificate, PEM |
| `GET /api/v1/tls/identity` | what the certificate claims, parsed |
| `GET /api/v1/chaos` | current chaos settings and fault counters |
| `PUT /api/v1/chaos` | replace chaos settings |
| `POST /api/v1/chaos/enable`, `POST /api/v1/chaos/disable` | master switch |
| `DELETE /api/v1/chaos/faults` | reset the counters |

`/api/v1/messages/{id}/html` is deliberately served on a sandboxed origin. Do not fetch it and
re-render the result inside your own page.

---

## 4. MCP

Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, on the same port as the inbox — one container, one port, one URL.

Read: `list_inboxes`, `list_recent_emails`, `search_emails`, `get_email`, `get_email_validation`,
`get_email_attachment`.

Destructive: `delete_email`, `clear_inbox`, `clear_all_inboxes`. These disappear from `tools/list`
entirely when `smtp-tester.mcp.allow-delete=false`, rather than failing at call time.

Chaos: `get_chaos_status`, `configure_chaos`, `reset_chaos_faults`.

Documentation: `get_documentation` returns this reference or the short `/llms.txt` index.

The usual flow is `list_inboxes` to discover addresses, `search_emails` to locate the message, then
`get_email` to read it. Validation findings come back as part of the ordinary message view, so
"did it arrive" and "was it correct" are one call, not two.

---

## 5. Validation

Every received message is checked against the RFCs and each finding carries a severity and the
rule it came from. `smtp-tester.validation.reject-on` decides what happens on the wire:

- `ERROR` (default) — a MUST-level violation is refused with `550` during the SMTP conversation.
- `WARNING` — SHOULD-level violations are refused too.
- `NONE` — everything is accepted, and every finding is still recorded and reported.

Rules cover the transport conversation, required and malformed headers, address syntax, MIME
structure and encoding, and TLS. Coming from MailHog, `ERROR` is the setting that will surprise
you: a fixture with no `Date:` header starts getting `550`s where it used to get `250`s. Start at
`NONE`, read the findings, then tighten.

Messages larger than `smtp-tester.smtp.max-message-size-bytes` are refused with `552 5.3.4`, and
the limit bounds the transfer itself rather than being advertised and then ignored.

DKIM (RFC 6376) is **not** verified. The enhanced status codes are reserved for it, but verifying a
signature requires a live DNS lookup, and a validator that behaves differently on a laptop, in CI
and offline is a worse default than not checking.

---

## 6. Chaos monkey

Transport-level fault injection, off by default, for testing how the application under test behaves
when its mail server misbehaves. Every probability is per-event, faults are counted, and
`smtp-tester.chaos.seed` fixes the random sequence so a failing run reproduces.

| Key | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.enabled` | `false` | master switch |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.accept-connection` | `0.99` | chance of **accepting** — note the inversion |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.disconnect` | `0.005` | drop the session with no reply |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.reject-sender` | `0.05` | refuse `MAIL FROM` with `451 4.3.0` |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.reject-recipient` | `0.05` | refuse `RCPT TO` with `451 4.3.0` |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.reject-auth` | `0.05` | fail `AUTH` |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.throttle` | `0.1` | rate-limit a transfer |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.min-bytes-per-second` | `1024` | slowest rate applied when throttling |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.max-bytes-per-second` | `10240` | fastest rate applied when throttling |
| `smtp-tester.chaos.seed` | *(none)* | fix the random sequence |

The rejection codes are transient (`4xx`) on purpose: a correct client retries them.

---

## 7. Every configuration key

Settable as a property, a `--flag`, or an environment variable. The environment form uppercases and
replaces separators: `smtp-tester.smtp.port` is `SMTP_TESTER_SMTP_PORT`.

| Key | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.enabled` | `true` | `false` runs the UI/API/MCP with no listener |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.port` | `1025` | `0` binds an ephemeral port |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.bind-address` | all interfaces | |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.host-name` | `smtp-tester` | announced in the SMTP greeting |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.max-message-size-bytes` | `26214400` | rejected with `552 5.3.4` |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.max-connections` | `200` | concurrent client connections |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.max-recipients` | `1000` | `RCPT TO` per transaction |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.connection-timeout` | `300000` | socket read timeout, milliseconds |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.accept-any-credentials` | `true` | any `AUTH` succeeds |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.tls.mode` | `OFF` | `OFF`, `OPTIONAL` or `REQUIRED` (STARTTLS) |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.tls.hostname` | `localhost` | the name the generated certificate is issued for |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.tls.keystore` | *(generated)* | PKCS#12 or JKS |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.tls.keystore-password` | *(none)* | password for that keystore |
| `smtp-tester.smtp.tls.key-alias` | *(none)* | which key in the keystore to present |
| `smtp-tester.store.max-messages` | `1000` | oldest evicted beyond this |
| `smtp-tester.spool.directory` | `/data/mail` in the container | empty disables writing to disk |
| `smtp-tester.spool.retention-interval` | `30s` | how often the background sweep trims the directory |
| `smtp-tester.spool.write-metadata` | `true` | also write `metadata.json` beside the raw message |
| `smtp-tester.spool.write-parts` | `true` | decoded MIME parts under `parts/` |
| `smtp-tester.spool.load-on-startup` | `true` | re-read the directory at boot |
| `smtp-tester.validation.enabled` | `true` | |
| `smtp-tester.validation.reject-on` | `ERROR` | `NONE`, `ERROR` or `WARNING` |
| `smtp-tester.mcp.enabled` | `true` | |
| `smtp-tester.mcp.allow-delete` | `true` | `false` hides the destructive tools |
| `smtp-tester.mcp.max-body-characters` | `20000` | bodies are truncated past this in tool output |
| `smtp-tester.mcp.default-limit` | `20` | page size for `list_recent_emails` when none is given |
| `smtp-tester.logging.enabled` | `true` | the structured per-message log line |
| `smtp-tester.logging.include-body` | `true` | turn off if bodies carry data you would rather not log |
| `smtp-tester.logging.max-body-characters` | `2000` | truncation point for the logged body |
| `smtp-tester.web.enabled` | `true` | |
| `smtp-tester.web.base-path` | `""` | mount the UI under a prefix |
| `smtp-tester.web.stream.enabled` | `true` | the server-sent events feed |
| `smtp-tester.web.stream.heartbeat` | `20s` | keep-alive interval on an idle stream |
| `smtp-tester.web.stream.max-subscribers` | `100` | beyond this, `503` |
| `smtp-tester.web.stream.replay-limit` | `100` | most messages one `since` replay may send |
| `server.port` | `8025` | UI, REST API and MCP |

---

## 8. The spool

With a spool directory configured, every accepted message is written to disk as it arrives. The
`.eml` files are byte-exact: no `Received:` header is inserted, so what is stored is what was sent.
Decoded MIME parts are written under `parts/` unless `write-parts` is off, and the directory is
re-read at startup so captured mail survives a restart.

The directory is bounded independently of the in-memory store, by a background sweep that runs
every `smtp-tester.spool.retention-interval` and trims it back to `store.max-messages`. Eviction
does not delete from disk inline, so between sweeps the spool can briefly hold more than the store
does — that is deliberate, to keep a recursive directory delete off the SMTP thread a client is
waiting on. Deleting a message explicitly, through the API or MCP, still removes its files
immediately.

---

## 9. Not built, deliberately

Each of these is a decision rather than a gap:

- **Running as a library inside a Spring Boot application.** Removed on purpose. Two shapes meant
  two bean graphs and two ways for a feature to work in one and quietly not the other.
- **A Maven plugin**, and **publishing to Maven Central**. Same reasoning; the image is the
  deliverable. Use the container, or run it from Testcontainers.
- **DKIM verification.** See section 5.
- **Message release / forwarding to a real SMTP server.** It would turn a mail sink into a relay on
  an unauthenticated API. The point of the tool is that mail cannot escape it.
- **HTTP basic auth on the UI and API.** SMTP on 1025 accepts any credentials by design, so a
  password on the inbox protects nothing port 1025 does not already give away.
- **Implicit TLS on a second port.** STARTTLS only, which is what submission clients expect.

---

## 10. Coming from MailHog or Mailpit

The ports and the SMTP behaviour match, so swapping the container is usually enough. Two things are
not drop-in. The HTTP API is a different shape — MailHog returns
`{ID, From:{Mailbox,Domain}, To[], Content, MIME, Raw}` and this returns the records documented
above, so anything written against MailHog's API needs porting. And validation rejects by default;
see section 5 for how to migrate without turning a passing suite red.
